before: Four limitations delimit the evidence and suggest concrete next steps. First, interval labels, efficiency and power measurement, interpolation, balancing, and rule-A settlement remain working interpretations; official clarification or metering specifications should precede any recalculation under different conventions. In particular, Q4-2 excludes Attachment 3 by an author interpretation, not an official prohibition. Second, surplus charging and issue-time reserve thresholds restrict the policy class, and the finite nonsmooth search has no global certificate; a subsequent study should compare richer causal control laws and independently bounded solutions on the same information set. Third, the fixed terminal proxy omits degradation and network dynamics; measured battery aging and network data would be needed to estimate those costs and test a longer horizon. Fourth, selection repeatedly used one historical year; genuinely untouched periods, prespecified comparisons, and matched tests of history windows, weights, capacity, and sustained forecast bias are needed before claiming robust future savings. None of these tests was performed for the current reserve controller.
after: Interval labels, efficiency and power measurement, interpolation, balancing, and rule-A settlement follow working conventions; official clarification or metering specifications would be needed before recalculating under different conventions. Richer causal controllers and independently bounded solutions should therefore be compared on the same information set. Untouched periods, prespecified comparisons, and matched tests of history windows, weights, capacity, and sustained forecast bias remain necessary.
